question: The length, breadth and height of a cuboid are in the ratio (2)/(3) : (1)/(4) : (5)/(6) . If the length, breadth and height of the cuboid are increased by 25\%, 33(1)/(3)\% and 40\% , respectively, then the volume of the new cuboid is how many times the volume of original cuboid?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert ratios: (2/3):(1/4):(5/6)

LCM = 12 ⇒ 8 : 3 : 10

Apply increase factors: 8×1.25 = 10, 3×4/3 = 4, 10×1.4 = 14

Old volume ratio = 8×3×10 = 240, New = 10×4×14 = 560

**∴ Answer = 560 ÷ 240 = 7/3 times**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of dimensions = (2/3) : (1/4) : (5/6)

Increase in length = 25%

Increase in breadth = 33 1/3%

Increase in height = 40%

**Formula used:**

Volume ∝ Length × Breadth × Height

**Calculation:**

⇒ Convert ratio into integers using LCM 12

⇒ Length : Breadth : Height = 8 : 3 : 10

⇒ New length = 8 × (1 + 25/100) = 8 × 5/4 = 10

⇒ New breadth = 3 × (1 + 1/3) = 3 × 4/3 = 4

⇒ New height = 10 × (1 + 40/100) = 10 × 7/5 = 14

⇒ Original volume = 8 × 3 × 10 = 240

⇒ New volume = 10 × 4 × 14 = 560

⇒ Ratio = 560 ÷ 240 = 7/3

**∴ The correct answer is 7/3 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cuboid

Volume = Length × Breadth × Height

Percentage Increase Formula

New value = Original × (1 + % increase/100)

Ratio Conversion

Fractions can be converted to integers using LCM

Multiplicative Effect

Total change in volume = product of individual scale factors
